races.name: Ebf Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (for Horses In Bands B, C And D) (Ebf Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Ric And Mary Hambro Aphrodite Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Brielle
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's consistent performer has a win and multiple places at 10-12f on good ground, and her natural front-running tendency means she will likely find herself racing in a more restrained midfield berth given how many prominent types are present — her STYLE_FIT score reflects a role that may not suit her best.

runners_data.name: Club Class
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's filly has been a model of consistency at 11-12f on standard ground but has yet to win from her five most recent runs; she wants to race prominently but the crowded forward positions in this field mean she faces a similar displacement challenge, and her OR of 81 puts her at a class disadvantage.

runners_data.name: Little Dorrit
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's hold-up filly has a sole win at 11f on Standard ground but has struggled to land a blow at 12f on Good in more recent efforts, and her last three runs at this trip on similar going produced finishes of 5th, 8th, and 4th — the controlled pace is not ideal for her late-running profile.

runners_data.name: Naga
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden's lightly-raced filly won back-to-back on good ground earlier in her career but her most recent start — 4th at 11f on good — suggests a slight stepping-stone effort; a natural front-runner who is unlikely to get close to Tribal Queen's early lead and will need to settle better than her instincts allow after 49 days off.

runners_data.name: Orionis
runners_data.note: William Haggas's filly has three wins from nine starts on good or good-to-firm ground and has been placed at 12f multiple times at Newmarket — track knowledge and course form are genuine positives, and she is one of the more likely horses to actually secure a forward position behind Tribal Queen.

runners_data.name: Revoir
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's OR-101 filly has been placed in four of her last five starts but has not won in that sequence; she is a genuine prominent type who will try to sit close to the pace, and her consistency makes her a live each-way contender if the race develops steadily, though the presence of headgear (p) suggests she needs keeping up to her work.

runners_data.name: Fashion's Fancy
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's lightly-raced three-year-old won on soft ground and finished third on Standard, giving her a limited but promising profile; headgear notes suggest she may settle in a hold-up role rather than attacking the pace, and 57 days between runs is worth monitoring, though Appleby's team typically present horses ready to run.

runners_data.name: K Sarra
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's three-year-old has just one win from four starts and her last outing was an 8th at 12f on soft ground — the step back to a firmer surface is potentially welcome, but her inconsistent form and a TS/RPR profile below the top-raters make her reliant on a strongly-run race she is unlikely to get here.

runners_data.name: Tribal Queen
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's OR-120 filly is the only confirmed front-runner in the field and should dictate from the outset on this flat track with no natural challenges to her position; her STYLE_FIT flag reflects the reality that leading a Listed field on fast ground carries its own pressures, but her class advantage at the head of affairs is the dominant structural factor in this race.

races.paceDynamic: Tribal Queen is the sole confirmed front-runner and, on Good to Firm ground over 1m4f on Newmarket's July course, she should be able to dictate at a sustainable gallop without meaningful pressure from the gate. Oriolis, Revoir, Naga, Brielle, and Club Class all carry prominent inclinations, but with five horses chasing one lead role, the map cannot accommodate them all — Tribal Queen and Orionis are best-placed to secure a forward berth, while Naga, Brielle, and Club Class will likely find themselves shuffled into roles behind their natural position. Fashion's Fancy, despite headgear notes suggesting a hold-up tendency, races for Appleby alongside stablemate Tribal Queen and could slot in comfortably off the pace as a genuine midfield-to-late traveller. The resulting shape is a controlled, honest gallop set by a high-rated front-runner on a flat, undemanding track, which structurally favours horses able to travel smoothly in the first half of the race and sustain a run from two furlongs out — the prominent-to-midfield profile that can switch off early and pick up when the pace is steady, rather than true deep closers who need a truly run race to get involved.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tribal Queen Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Tribal Queen dictates an uncontested, metronomic gallop and the pack settles in behind without disruption.
scenarios.body: Tribal Queen sets a fair but not fast pace from the front, and the race unfolds as a procession into the home straight where class and a clean run from prominent positions decide it; horses who can travel just off the pace and accelerate over the final two furlongs are ideally suited.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Scramble Lifts Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If the cluster of natural front-runners — Naga, Brielle, Orionis — push forward early and force a genuinely contested pace.
scenarios.body: The early positional battle produces a stronger-than-expected gallop that stretches the field, burning off horses who use too much energy getting their place; those who settle kindly in mid-division and conserve their run benefit most in the final quarter-mile.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Class Closer Picks Up Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough that the field strings out and hold-up runners get daylight turning in.
scenarios.body: Little Dorrit or K Sarra, racing from off the pace, encounter clear ground earlier than usual and sustain their run to the line as front-runners tie up; this is the least structurally likely shape given the controlled pace setting.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Favours Bold Move
scenarios.trigger: If Tribal Queen's gallop is so modest that the race turns into a sprint and a horse who makes a bold move two furlongs out catches the field flat-footed.
scenarios.body: A very slow early tempo compresses the field into a bunch, and the horse with the most tactical speed who commits first from a forward position secures a lead they are never caught; class and rating advantage matter most in this shape.

watchPoints.text: Tribal Queen's uncontested lead is the pivotal tactical factor — if she controls the pace from the front without being challenged, horses who need a truly run race will find themselves with nowhere to go in the home straight.

Naga, Brielle, and Club Class are all natural prominent runners who cannot all get their preferred position — monitor the first furlong for any scrimmaging or early energy expenditure that could compromise their chance at the business end.

Fashion's Fancy's headgear note and 57-day absence for Appleby warrant watching in the early stages — if she fails to settle cleanly from an unfamiliar hold-up position the race could unfold in a way that leaves her out of contention.

Little Dorrit and K Sarra both require a strongly-run race to produce their best, and the controlled pace Tribal Queen is likely to set means both hold-up runners face a structural disadvantage — watch to see whether they can find a clear passage despite racing into what may be a steady-gallop bunch.

Orionis's Newmarket course form (two wins at 12f on good) makes her worth watching as a horse likely to secure an early prominent position behind the pace-setter — if she travels smoothly through the race, she becomes the most dangerous stalker in the field.

races.name: Lettergold Plastics Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Flag Of St George
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with two wins at Newmarket over 7f, most recently placed twice in similar company; 169 days off the track is the notable concern, though Jane Chapple-Hyam's 2/15 14-day strike rate suggests the yard isn't firing at its sharpest, and Paddy Bradley takes the ride on a horse who handles this going well.

runners_data.name: I Still Have Faith
runners_data.note: Regular front-of-field performer who handles Good ground on this course and has placed three times in the last 15 similar-going runs; Stuart Williams runs two here and Ray Dawson's booking is the senior jockey in the yard's pair, though a form string of 625406 raises questions about current peak form.

runners_data.name: Warrior Mode
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse returning after 255 days off the track — a significant absence for a handicapper — with Sir Mark Prescott sending him out fresh, which the yard does effectively; won over 7f at Sandown on similar ground but will need luck in running from the rear on this wide, unobstructed course.

runners_data.name: Bell Shot
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's seven-year-old has placed four times in his last 15 similar-going runs and showed a good effort (3rd, 7f, Good) recently; he is a natural hold-up horse who will find himself racing closer to the pace than suits him given the field composition, which the STYLE_FIT tag reflects honestly.

runners_data.name: Where's Freddy
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams's second string on the day, 38 days since last run and with a patchy recent string including two 10th-placed efforts over 8f; a genuine hold-up horse who will not get his ideal position and whose best recent effort came over 7f Good — the step back in trip is potentially positive but the race shape is against him.

runners_data.name: Jumby
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up specialist who has failed to place in his last four runs over 7f on Good or Soft, and his form string of 640-80 makes for sober reading; Oliver Carmichael's 7lb claim is a practical aid but this horse needs a truly troubled pace to make ground and that is unlikely under Miletus.

runners_data.name: Miletus
runners_data.note: James Keane's five-year-old has the key profile fact of a recent Newmarket 7f win on Good going and will lead from the front; the STYLE_FIT discount applies if his chance depends on being tracked — as the front-runner he is racing fully in role and his prominence is entirely natural, making him a genuine player if his stamina holds on the run-in.

races.paceDynamic: Miletus is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival for the lead among the prominent types, is set to dictate an uncontested, controlled gallop across Newmarket's July Course seven furlongs. Flag Of St George and I Still Have Faith will push forward to track Miletus closely, creating an orthodox prominent-held shape rather than a contested burn-up, which suits those with tactical speed over late acceleration. The hold-up horses — Jumby, Warrior Mode, Bell Shot, and Where's Freddy — will be forced to wait for a gap in the final two furlongs, and on a course that rewards those travelling prominently on Good to Firm ground, the race shape strongly favours runners who can sit just off the pace and pounce in the straight rather than deep closers waiting for a collapse that may never come. Note that Bell Shot and Where's Freddy are genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map because the field holds more true rear-runners than the visual can accommodate; Jumby and Warrior Mode are more likely to secure the rearmost berths in reality.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Miletus Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Miletus sets a fair but uncontested gallop and the prominent trackers pick the right moment turning in.
scenarios.body: Miletus dictates on the front end without pressure, setting a tempo that suits those racing within a length or two; Flag Of St George and I Still Have Faith are ideally placed to sprint off his back in the final two furlongs on this sharp, flat track.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Reel Them In
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final furlong and closers find a clear run through.
scenarios.body: Miletus's comfortable lead becomes vulnerable only if the early fractions were faster than they appeared, allowing Warrior Mode or Jumby to come through late; this requires a clear passage on a course where traffic can cost closers dearly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Miletus Front-Runs Entire
scenarios.trigger: If Miletus sustains his gallop all the way to the line having stolen a decisive advantage through the dip.
scenarios.body: A lone front-runner on a flat, fair track in Good to Firm conditions can occasionally steal a race if the pace behind is not properly coordinated; Miletus has a recent win over this exact trip and going at Newmarket to his name.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Competitive Scramble Develops
scenarios.trigger: If Flag Of St George or I Still Have Faith challenges Miletus earlier than expected, forcing a genuine pace battle.
scenarios.body: A faster tempo would bring the hold-up horses into play and create a more open finish; Bell Shot has course form and experience to capitalise if a genuine scrap develops, though racing outside his natural zone tempers confidence.

watchPoints.text: Watch Miletus in the early stages — if he steals two lengths unchallenged past the two-furlong pole, prominent horses Flag Of St George and I Still Have Faith must close immediately or the race is gone.

Flag Of St George has been off 169 days and a strip of track fitness, not just ability, will determine whether she quickens late; if she misses the break or travels flat, her position advantage evaporates.

Bell Shot and Where's Freddy are both natural hold-up horses who will be drawn into a midfield position they don't prefer — watch for either rider switching wide early to manufacture racing room and whether they can sustain their effort to the line from an unnatural berth.

Warrior Mode's 255-day absence makes his initial response over the first furlong key — Prescott horses often need that first run back, and if he travels kindly from the outset he may be sharper than his layoff suggests.

Going is confirmed Good to Firm for this race despite the header showing Good — the fast surface marginally favours prominent racers who can maintain momentum rather than late closers needing softness underfoot.

races.name: Club 26 At Ascot Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Westmorian
runners_data.note: Has been running prominently but the STYLE_FIT flag tempers confidence — seven-year-old in modest form (0W0P in similar going), and Grant Tuer's yard is 4/11 in the 14-day window; value here is primarily as race-shaper rather than winner.|

runners_data.name: Yes I'm Mali
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope takes the ride on a four-year-old with a strong course-and-distance record (1W3P in similar going over 6f), returning 14 days after his last outing in fine form — a genuine contender who naturally wants to come from off the pace and should find a clean run on the wide Newmarket straight.|

runners_data.name: Expert Agent
runners_data.note: Two wins at this course and distance in good-to-firm conditions make him the most compelling profile in the field — Marco Ghiani rides a six-year-old who is returning on 28 days' rest and has place strikes in six of his last fifteen similar-going runs; a hold-up type who should find the July straight suits his finishing style.|

runners_data.name: Fenlander
runners_data.note: Hat-trick seeker on the back of three consecutive 6f wins at Goodwood, returning on 23 days, with 11 places from 15 similar-going runs — Christian Howarth's 3lb claim is a bonus, and a prominent racing style means he should secure a clean stalking position behind Westmorian without being shuffled back.|

runners_data.name: Dashing Dick
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon partners an eight-year-old who is a genuine hold-up horse in reality, though the redistribution note means he is unlikely to get his preferred position at the rear; his recent form shows nothing better than third since 2023, and 0W in similar going across 12 attempts is a significant concern.|

runners_data.name: Lili Marleen
runners_data.note: Hector Crouch rides a four-year-old returning after 79 days off — the lengthy absence is the primary flag, and her historical form is mostly over 8f or more on AW, meaning both the distance and turf surface represent genuine unknowns; the ⚠ fades-in-finish tag compounds the concern for a hold-up horse on this shape.|

runners_data.name: Spring Bloom
runners_data.note: John Butler's nine-year-old is a model of consistency in placed efforts (0W5P in similar going) but has never converted; David Probert steers a mare who naturally wants to come late but will be crowded at the rear by several similar types — the age and lack of a win make her a place rather than win profile.|

runners_data.name: Generous Rascal
runners_data.note: Three-year-old wearing a hood for Dylan Cunha's yard, which is 0/13 in the 14-day window — the booking of Luke Morris is workmanlike rather than inspiring, and a form string of three consecutive placed efforts without winning suggests a horse that runs well to a point but struggles to land the blow.|

races.paceDynamic: Westmorian is the one confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead identified, should be able to set a controlled, sustainable gallop over this flat Newmarket July course 6f. Fenlander and Generous Rascal will push forward prominently behind, creating a small group across the early stages but without the firepower to seriously pressure Westmorian's early fractions. The pace is therefore likely to be honest rather than scorching — a tempo that rewards those who can travel into it and produce a clean finishing effort rather than those waiting for a searching burn-up. On this shape, hold-up horses carrying a genuine late kick are theoretically set up, but the field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Yes I'm Mali, Expert Agent, Dashing Dick, Lili Marleen, and Spring Bloom all want to come from off the pace, meaning several will be forced wider or closer to the pace than ideal, diluting the late-runner advantage; the runners most likely to actually secure a genuine tracking position are Yes I'm Mali and Expert Agent given their stronger form profiles and jockey quality. A controlled, uncontested pace with a prominent/tracking profile — horses racing close enough to pounce without being caught in traffic — is the profile this shape most clearly favours.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Westmorian dictates an uncontested, even pace and the prominent/tracking horses travel comfortably into the final 2f.
scenarios.body: Westmorian sets the fractions, Fenlander and Generous Rascal sit in behind, and a horse travelling just off the pace has enough cover to produce a sustained finish on the July course straight. Fenlander, in red-hot form with three consecutive wins, is ideally placed to punch off the shoulder and sustain the run to the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Cuts Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just brisk enough to string the field out and a genuine late-runner finds a clear passage through the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Yes I'm Mali and Expert Agent both carry strong course-and-distance profiles in this going and have the raw form to deliver a late challenge if the fractions open up space on the wide Newmarket straight. Expert Agent in particular has two wins at this course and distance in similar conditions and would be the primary beneficiary of a clean run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Runner Outstays
scenarios.trigger: If Westmorian is able to slow the race to a near-crawl and converts a truly sapping finish into a sprint that only the leader can sustain.
scenarios.body: A dawdling gallop benefits the horse on the front end who can control the pace and quicken from a near-standstill, leaving hold-up types with no momentum to reel them in. Westmorian, despite modest recent form, would be the direct beneficiary if granted a completely uncontested lead and a slow-burn tempo.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos, Outsider Quickens
scenarios.trigger: If the congestion of multiple hold-up horses racing out of role creates interference in the straight and a lightly-weighted runner finds the gaps first.
scenarios.body: Spring Bloom's consistent placed record in this going and distance profile means she could pick up pieces if the finish unravels amid a bunched mid-race, though the weight of evidence does not strongly support this shape materialising. Generous Rascal, wearing a hood and with three consecutive placed efforts at this trip, represents the other unexpected beneficiary.

watchPoints.text: Fenlander's hat-trick bid is the most significant form angle in the race — watch whether Christian Howarth allows him to travel smoothly behind Westmorian rather than being pushed forward to lead, as an overcrowded early pace could compromise his finishing effort.

Expert Agent's 28-day absence and market moves in the hour before the race deserve close attention — a well-backed Expert Agent, given two prior wins at this course and distance in these conditions, would signal trainer confidence in a return to form.

Lili Marleen's 79-day layoff combined with a fades-in-finish flag makes her a significant risk; if she drifts in the market she is unlikely to be a factor and backers of hold-up horses in the scenario should monitor whether she is supported or dismissed.

Watch the early strides to confirm whether Westmorian actually leads uncontested — if Generous Rascal or Fenlander push forward aggressively from the gate, the pace dynamic shifts from controlled to pressed, which materially changes the probabilities for Scenarios A and B.

Spring Bloom and Dashing Dick, both genuine hold-up types forced into midfield roles, may cause interference in the straight as they try to weave through — any horse tracking wide and clear of this potential traffic in the final 2f will hold a tactical advantage.

races.name: National Stud "Confined" Handicap Stakes (For Horses With No More Than One Win)

runners_data.name: Ziggy's Avenger
runners_data.note: Landed a win over 8f on Good at Newmarket in July (sim-going form solid: 3 wins/places from 6) and Hector Crouch rides for a trainer in decent 14-day form; a natural hold-up type who should sit comfortably at the rear of this slow-tempo contest before deploying what looked a smart turn of foot in recent outings — the step up to 10f is the question mark but Bell horses often improve for the extra furlong.

runners_data.name: Flag Of Eva
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's three-year-old has run exclusively on Good or Soft ground and placed twice in three starts, suggesting a consistent type; a genuine hold-up runner who will likely settle furthest back, and the step up from 8f to 10f on good-to-firm looks a logical progression for a filly who has travelled well before fading — watch whether she sees out the trip.

runners_data.name: Madjid
runners_data.note: Harry Charlton sends this one out in good recent form (2 from 14 in 14-day window) and Cieren Fallon is a strong booking at Newmarket; in truth a hold-up horse by nature who has been squeezed into a mapped midfield position by the congested style profile — he will need to be closer to the pace than he naturally prefers, which tempers confidence slightly, though his 10f form on Good is consistent.

runners_data.name: John Harrison
runners_data.note: David Probert partners this Alan King gelding who has placed twice at up to 8f, and the step to 10f here is a significant factor to assess; his hold-up style means he belongs further back than the midfield map position suggests, effectively racing out of his natural role in this shape, which slightly discounts his chance — his best form came over shorter on a more conventional pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Pipily
runners_data.note: T J Kent's runner is making a step up in trip having run exclusively at 6-8f, including on Soft ground where she has placed — the Good to Firm at Newmarket is firmer than anything in her form, which is a genuine concern; her hold-up profile is being mapped into midfield by necessity rather than inclination, and a 32-day break combined with an untested trip and going concern makes her among the harder horses to assess in this field.

runners_data.name: Moon Warp
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's yard is in strong 14-day form (3/12) but Moon Warp returns from a 318-day absence — a significant flag — and carries a tagged tendency to fade in the finish, which is a real liability in what will be a pure sprint finish; the horse's all-weather form at 7-8f does not obviously translate to 10f on fast turf, and her hold-up style being mapped outward into midfield compounds an already difficult profile to trust.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in the field, this 1m2f contest at Newmarket's July course is set to develop into a slowly-run, bunched affair where the pace is manufactured from necessity rather than intent. Every runner in this six-horse field holds a hold-up profile, meaning the early gallop will almost certainly be pedestrian as jockeys wait for others to commit — on Good to Firm ground at Newmarket, that creates a premium on late acceleration over the final two furlongs. The race is likely to drift into a sprint finish from the Bushes, with the winner emerging from whoever possesses the sharpest turn of foot or is best placed rounding the final bend. This shape decisively favours the horse who can travel smoothly in a slowly-run race and produce a clean, sustained finish — a classic flat-track closer profile on good ground suits best. The field holds more genuine hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear; Madjid, John Harrison, and Pipily are the most likely to actually push forward and secure a midfield berth, but none are natural front-runners so the early pace will remain modest regardless.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slow throughout and the race becomes a dash for home from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: With six hold-up types crawling through the early stages on good-to-firm ground, the Newmarket straight becomes a flat sprint where acceleration off a slow tempo is everything; runners who can quicken cleanly from the rear without cover issues will dominate.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Mover Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one horse travels notably better than rivals through a falsely-run race and picks them off entering the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A horse who secures a good position rounding the dip and travels kindly through the slowly-run contest can simply outclass rivals for finishing pace when the gap opens; the Newmarket straight rewards those who time their run without being squeezed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Pair Steal It
scenarios.trigger: If one or two runners, pushed wide by congestion at the rear, end up on or near the lead and steal a march going into the straight.
scenarios.body: A slow gallop can paradoxically hand the advantage to a horse who finds itself unexpectedly prominent — if Madjid or Pipily drift forward and set a modest pace, a front-two combination can hold on as the pack fails to coordinate a late challenge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closer Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If a genuinely strong pace develops by accident and sets up a true late run for the hold-up horses at the back.
scenarios.body: Moon Warp aside — who carries a noted tendency to fade in the finish and is deeply disadvantaged here — a horse who has been held up furthest back and produces a sustained gallop through the final quarter-mile could run through beaten rivals; however, this scenario depends on horses racing authentically out of role and is the least likely shape to materialise.

watchPoints.text: Moon Warp's 318-day absence combined with a noted tendency to fade late makes her a significant market-watch runner — if she is well-backed, it suggests connections have done serious home work that contradicts her visible form profile.

With no natural front-runner, watch the first furlong closely: if Madjid or Pipily push forward under instruction rather than instinct, they effectively set the shape of the entire race and transform Scenario C from unlikely to live.

Ziggy's Avenger's recent win over 8f on Good at Newmarket is the standout piece of course-and-going form — if Hector Crouch secures a clean passage turning into the straight, he becomes the most dangerous finisher in a sprint scenario.

The Good to Firm going (official report confirms 4:52 at Good to Firm) is meaningfully faster than any ground Pipily has encountered — monitor whether connections accept or whether a market drift signals connections are cautious about conditions.

John Harrison's drop from a 2/7f placed effort down to a midfield map position masks a hold-up profile that is being asked to race closer than ideal — if the pace is genuinely slow, his inability to dictate his own rhythm could cost him the chance his form on paper suggests he merits.

races.name: Lodge At The National Stud Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Elan d'Or
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Stuart Williams, wins best from the front and has two wins at 7f on Standard ground; her Good-to-Firm record is limited (0W2P from 2) and stepping to 1m for the first time is an open question, but she holds the key tactical card as sole pace-setter.

runners_data.name: Lady Mariko
runners_data.note: Dylan Cunha runner with a naturally prominent style and course form at 1m; her best recent effort was a sixth at this trip on Good ground and she has form figures of 2W3P on similar going, making her a plausible stalker who could benefit if Elan d'Or is caught late.

runners_data.name: Silca Bay
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton sends this mare back quickly (15 days) having run fourth here at 1m on Good ground; naturally a front-runner by inclination but with more pace types in this field she is likely to be pushed into a less comfortable midfield berth — her 0W0P on similar going tempers expectation.

runners_data.name: Dovey Moon
runners_data.note: Four wins at 1m on Good ground make the trip and conditions ideal for this David Evans four-year-old, and he has genuine speed; however, he is a true prominent racer who cannot get to the front in this company, and racing against his grain from a midfield position is a complication despite his strong course-and-distance profile.

runners_data.name: Astrazar
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's lightly-raced three-year-old with back-to-back wins including a 1m win on Heavier ground; his Good-to-Firm profile (1W3P) is solid and Hector Crouch rides for a yard in form (6/33 14-day), making him the most natural beneficiary of a close-tracking role behind the leader.

runners_data.name: Rogue Encore
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 106 days off for Peter Chapple-Hyam, whose yard has just 0/1 in the 14-day window; his Standtrack form is poor on similar going (0W1P from 3 at this trip) and a moderate pace with only seven runners makes it very hard for a true closer to find the gaps he needs.

runners_data.name: Mythical Guest
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up performer for George Margarson, running just 8 days after his last start; has 0W4P on Good going at 1m and is consistent without winning, but a controlled pace set by Elan d'Or in a small field will likely see him finishing into minor placings rather than challenging for the spoils.

races.paceDynamic: Elan d'Or is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she should slot onto the front and control a measured, sustainable gallop over Newmarket's July course mile. Lady Mariko and Astrazar will push to sit prominently behind her, creating a compact front group but without the pressure that would turn this into a true test of stamina. The field contains more prominent-minded horses than the shape can accommodate — Silca Bay and Dovey Moon are both natural front-runners who will struggle to find their true position and will be shuffled into a midfield slot against their instincts. The result is a race likely run at a controlled, even tempo that sets up best for a prominent racer who travels smoothly into contention and quickens from a good position — hold-up horses Rogue Encore and Mythical Guest face a stiff task if the pace is never truly strong enough to bring them into play late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Elan d'Or Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Elan d'Or gets away smartly and dictates an uncontested, moderate gallop with the field strung behind her.
scenarios.body: She sets a rhythm that suits her strengths, and horses who track closely in the slipstream get the clearest run to challenge at the two-furlong pole; the moderate pace never generates the late surge that would bring hold-up horses into contention.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Scramble Quickens
scenarios.trigger: If Silca Bay or Dovey Moon push forward aggressively early and force a contested pace against Elan d'Or.
scenarios.body: A more pressured gallop through the middle stages stretches the field sooner, suiting horses with tactical speed and the ability to travel wide of trouble; those who race out of role may still find enough if the early heat weakens the leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is faster than expected and the front group ties up inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A genuine end-to-end gallop would bring the hold-up horses into the race for the first time, but both Rogue Encore and Mythical Guest need conditions they have not reliably found on similar going, making this scenario fragile by nature.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Crawl Bunches Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses to a near-walk and the race becomes a sprint for home from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: A bunched sprint suits the horse with the sharpest turn of foot regardless of style, but this outcome is unlikely given Elan d'Or's preference for front-running and the competitive nature of a handicap field.

watchPoints.text: If Silca Bay or Dovey Moon break sharply and challenge Elan d'Or for the lead in the first two furlongs, the pace dynamic changes entirely and hold-up horses become live players for the first time.
Rogue Encore's 106-day absence is a significant fitness flag — watch his early movement and how quickly Luke Morris has to push for position; a rusty run here would be no surprise.

Dovey Moon's record of 4 wins at 1m on Good ground is highly relevant, but if J F Egan cannot find a way to travel prominently despite the race shape, his finishing kick may arrive too late on a track that rewards forward positioning.

Good-to-Firm conditions throughout the card suggest the ground is riding faster than the official Good description — horses with proven fast-ground form (Lady Mariko, Astrazar) may hold an advantage over those whose best form has come on softer surfaces (Silca Bay's sole win came on Soft).
